subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Invasive Mole, Choriocarcinoma and Placental Site Tumour

steps.tx: Molar villi invading deeply into myometrium and vessels form an **invasive mole**. It almost always follows a molar pregnancy and rarely spreads beyond the pelvis. Chemotherapy cures it while preserving fertility in nearly all cases. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Invasive mole grows molar villi into myometrium and cures with chemotherapy preserving fertility.

steps.tx: A malignant trophoblast tumour without villi, spreading early through blood, is **choriocarcinoma**. It can follow mole, miscarriage, term pregnancy or ectopic gestation. Haemorrhagic metastases to lung, vagina and brain are characteristic. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Choriocarcinoma spreads early through blood without villi to lung, vagina and brain.

steps.tx: Round cannonball deposits in the lungs on chest imaging are **cannonball metastases**. They are the commonest metastatic presentation of choriocarcinoma. Despite their dramatic appearance, they melt away with chemotherapy remarkably. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Cannonball metastases fill the lungs in choriocarcinoma yet melt with chemotherapy.

steps.tx: A rare slow tumour of intermediate trophoblast producing mainly placental lactogen is **placental site trophoblastic tumour**. Hormone levels are low relative to tumour bulk, and chemotherapy resistance is typical. Hysterectomy is the mainstay for uterine confined disease. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Placental site tumour produces little hormone, resists chemotherapy, and needs hysterectomy.

steps.tx: Vaginal metastases are highly vascular and must never be biopsied, a rule of **no vaginal biopsy**. Biopsy can unleash uncontrollable haemorrhage. Diagnosis rests on hormone levels and imaging instead. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Vaginal metastases must never be biopsied because uncontrollable haemorrhage can follow.

steps.tx: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is staged anatomically from uterus confined to distant spread, termed **FIGO staging**. Stage combines with the prognostic score to choose single or multi agent chemotherapy. This dual system is unique to this disease. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: FIGO staging plus prognostic score together choose chemotherapy intensity in this disease.

steps.tx: Brain metastases need intrathecal or high dose systemic methotrexate within **multi agent regimens**. Whole brain radiation is now largely avoided. Even stage four disease cures in most women treated at specialist centres. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Brain metastases use high dose methotrexate regimens, and most stage four disease still cures.

steps.tx: Hysterectomy retains a role for chemo resistant uterine disease and uncontrolled bleeding, termed **salvage surgery**. It also suits older women who have completed families with uterus confined disease. Fertility sparing remains default for the young. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Salvage surgery with hysterectomy treats chemo resistant uterine disease and uncontrolled bleeding.

steps.tx: Cure is declared after sustained normal hormone with surveillance continuing for years, called **remission follow up**. Late relapses are rare but described, especially after high risk disease. Pregnancy after chemotherapy usually proceeds normally. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Remission follow up continues for years, and pregnancy after chemotherapy usually proceeds normally.
